spawnSpread.description: How many different numbers a new block can show. The game's own (4) deals one of the four values up to the highest it unlocks (maxBlock, 3 at the start, rising as bigger blocks are made). 2 deals only the top two, 6 the top six (never below 1), uniformly. Fewer different numbers mean more neighbours match. Applies to blocks spawned from now on.
spawnSpread.adjustment_guide: The main difficulty lever. Lower (2-3) for relax and joy or a player who keeps running out of moves; raise (5-6) for grit and planning once the player reaches high numbers reliably. Change by 1 at a time.

startBoardSpread.description: Highest number on the starting board. The board's values run from 1 to this, with 1 twice as likely as each of the others (the game's own board is 1-3). Lower values give an easy start with many matches; higher values a mixed, harder start. Applies from the next game start or restart.
startBoardSpread.adjustment_guide: Sets how hard the opening is. 2 for an easy, match-rich start; 4-6 for grit, or to make groups harder to spot. Takes effect on the next restart.

adjustment_instructions:
Impossible 10 is a merge puzzle on a 5x5 board of numbered blocks: tapping a group of touching blocks with the same number merges them into one block one higher; new blocks drop in from the top. The goal is a 10 (LEVEL_COMPLETE); the game ends when no two neighbours match (LEVEL_FAILED).
Levers: spawnSpread sets how many different numbers new blocks can show (fewer = more matches = easier); startBoardSpread sets the highest number on the starting board (lower = easier opening; applies on the next restart).
- relax: spawnSpread 2-3, startBoardSpread 2-3.
- focus: spawnSpread 4, startBoardSpread 3 (the game's own balance).
- grit: spawnSpread 5-6, startBoardSpread 4-6; lower spawnSpread by 1 after repeated quick LEVEL_FAILED events.
- joy: spawnSpread 2-3, startBoardSpread 3, so merges come often and the numbers climb toward 10.
Change one lever at a time, by 1. Several LEVEL_FAILED events with low MERGE block values mean the game is too hard; LEVEL_COMPLETE soon after a start means it is too easy.
skill_adjustment_instructions:
Impossible 10 trains Planning and Problem Solving (setting up merges that lead to bigger ones) and Pattern Recognition (spotting groups of matching numbers).
- planning, problem-solving: spawnSpread 5-6 with startBoardSpread 3-4, so the player has to set up chains in advance.
- pattern-recognition: startBoardSpread 4-5 with spawnSpread 4, so groups are harder to spot.
Ease spawnSpread back by 1 when runs keep ending early.
notes: Impossible 10's difficulty knobs, matching static/skillprintShim.js, ../parameters.json and GameAdjustmentTester's 'impossible-10' keys.
